subtitle: Lesson 12 · Network Architecture at Enterprise Scale

steps.label: 3 teams peering directly: 9 connections, easy to review
steps.sub: a reasonable design for the team count at the time

steps.label: 30 teams, same approach: ~435 potential connections
steps.sub: overlapping IP ranges, no single place to answer "can team 14 reach team 22?"

steps.label: Nothing was wrong at the time — nothing forced a revisit
steps.sub: the design had no built-in answer for what happens as N grows

eyebrow: Principle one: a central address plan
code:
# reserved supernet: 10.0.0.0/8
# hub:          10.0.0.0/16
# spoke pool:   10.1.0.0/16 - 10.255.0.0/16, /20 per spoke
#   spoke-finance:    10.1.0.0/20
#   spoke-platform:   10.2.0.0/20
#   spoke-analytics:  10.3.0.0/20
caption: Allocate CIDR before provisioning a spoke, not after — overlap is the most common cause of a redesign.

eyebrow: Principle two: a standardized spoke template
code:
module "spoke" {
  source       = "git::https://devops/terraform-modules//spoke-network"
  spoke_name   = "analytics"
  cidr_block   = "10.3.0.0/20"
  hub_vnet_id  = module.hub.vnet_id
  dns_zone_id  = module.hub.private_dns_zone_id
}
caption: Every spoke gets the same CIDR source, hub connectivity, routing, and DNS link — no reinventing it per team.

steps.label: Deny spoke-to-spoke by default
steps.sub: adding spoke 31 never requires re-auditing spokes 1 through 30

steps.label: Central team owns the hub, DNS, IP plan, spoke template
steps.sub: the things that create risk if every team owns its own version

steps.label: Each team owns what's inside its own spoke
steps.sub: central review for everything inside a spoke makes the platform team a bottleneck
